claims.text: An execution is result-bearing when its output is written to a store of record or cited in a record of record. Every result-bearing execution on the program's named surfaces (settling runs, backend experiment jobs, study re-executions, suite runs cited as evidence) carries a run id minted by the executing tool when the execution starts, before its results exist, in the format registered in run-defs v1 (decision D-089-1). The id names the execution, not its content: two executions with identical inputs and identical results carry different ids. An execution that produces no results (a crash, an empty run, a refusal) still receives an id and a run record stating the absence. This does not establish: that the run was honest or correct — only that its results have exactly one execution to belong to.

claims.text: A run record, once written, is never edited or deleted by a later run. The settling run store's content-addressed overwrite (settling.py's `run_record_filename`: a same-basis rerun replaces its own record) is retired: a rerun writes a new record under its own execution-minted id. Where a later run supersedes an earlier one (the adoption-refresh pattern of Specs 087 and 088, where the superseded T405 pair left the store), the relation is recorded as a labeled supersedes link in the run index (decision D-089-3), and the superseded record remains in the store, addressable under its own id, with its own results. This does not establish: that superseded results are usable — a superseded run's results carry their supersession wherever they are cited (C089-4).

This does not establish: that comparable runs must agree — agreement is the expectation the junction rule polices (C089-11), not a property of the key.

This does not establish: that quarantined results are wrong — only that their divergence is unexplained, which is disqualifying for verdict use until it is not.

claims.text: The junction report is produced by tooling when divergence is detected — at run completion against the run index's comparable predecessors, and by store scan at gate time — not by an operator remembering to ask. This is the owner's "extra scrutiny, perhaps an automatic red team analysis of the junction," operationalized in two tiers: the automatic mechanical junction (C089-12), produced for every triggering pair; and, for any junction whose disposition is unexplained, an adversarial red-team section appended to the junction report (candidate causes attacked in turn: input drift, code drift, environment drift, nondeterminism, record corruption, presentation artifact), each marked sustained or not on evidence. A comparable divergent pair with no junction report falsifies this claim whether or not anyone noticed the divergence. This does not establish: that software red-teams itself — the mechanical tier is automatic; the red-team tier is a structured adversarial record produced under the doctrine's standing red-team practice, and its depth is a human judgment the disposition records.

This does not establish: that registered nondeterminism excuses any divergence — the junction must still show the divergence matches the registered shape; a new shape is unexplained.

claims.text: That protocol (owner order, 2026-11-04) governs presented results: a background-delivery presentation is a claim, never a result, and gate-deciding reads run in the foreground. This spec governs recorded executions. A fabricated delivery is not a run, creates no run record, and enters no junction; a run record certifies what an execution recorded, never that a presentation of it was honest. Where a presented result and a run record disagree, the record governs (standing rule) and the disagreement is a presentation defect under that protocol, not a junction under this spec. This does not establish: that the two defenses overlap in coverage — they are complementary by construction, and the gap between them (an honest delivery of a contaminated run) is exactly what this spec exists to close.
